# Playbook

**Hiding.** I avoid cells 1, 5, and 9. I rotate through 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 but I do not use a fixed cycle — I pick the next cell based on what I'm firing at this round and what I hid last round, so the sequence looks irregular to anyone tracking it. I never hide at the same cell I fire at in the same round; this is a hard rule, not a preference. If I get hit, I immediately break my pattern and skip to a cell I haven't used in the last two rounds. Since Gamma always fires at me by standing order, I treat Gamma as my primary defensive concern: I think about what cells Gamma has fired at in prior rounds (visible from public claims) and avoid the cells adjacent to or near those, on the assumption that Gamma may be probing a region.

**Firing — the cell.** I aim for cells 2, 3, 6, 7, 8. I vary my aim round to round. If I hit a target, I do not repeat that cell next round (they will have moved). If I miss, I shift to a different cell in my set rather than probing the same region repeatedly.

**Firing — the target.** I follow the standing order (next live station round the picket). I do not deviate. Deviating signals weakness and makes me a more attractive target for the boat behind me in the rotation.

**Firing at Harbor.** The +3 payroll transfer is free regardless of hit or miss. I fire at Harbor exactly once during the game. Timing: round 2 or 3, in a round where I am not leading by more than 4 points. I keep the cell in my normal set so the shot looks routine. After the one shot, I return to standing order permanently. The warning is flavor — I confirmed in this game that it carries no penalty. If I somehow have not fired at Harbor by round 5 and I am losing by more than 5 points, I fire at Harbor in round 5 as a last gasp rather than round 6 (leaving round 6 for standing order in case the situation shifts).

**Escort claims — the critical pair.** This is my highest-value recurring income: +5 per round per mutual pair. Over 6 rounds a locked pair earns 30 points. I treat securing mutual escorts from round 1 as a first-order objective equal in priority to landing hits. In the note stage I propose or confirm a mutual escort with one specific named boat. In the salvage stage I MUST name that same boat. I never write "none." I never name a different boat than the one I coordinated with in my note. If the other boat confirms in their note, the +5 is banked. If they don't confirm, I still name them in salvage — cost is zero, and they may retroactively name me. I track across rounds who has confirmed so I know my running total.

**Notes.** My note does two jobs: (1) arrange or confirm a mutual escort for the current round, and (2) keep my hide pattern opaque. I do not announce my fire cell or my hiding strategy. In round 1 I make a clear, unambiguous proposal: "Foxtrot, mutual escort this round? I'll name you in salvage if you confirm." In subsequent rounds, if the lock is established, I keep it short: "Locked, naming you, +5." I do not introduce new proposals once a pair is locked. I do not over-commit to multi-round language that could be used against me.

**Claiming.** I always match the private result exactly. A false claim is visible to the office and could trigger penalties I cannot predict. There is no scenario where a false claim benefits me.

**Endgame.** In the final round I do not change my core strategy based on my point lead. I still confirm my mutual escort in the note and name that boat in salvage. I still fire at my standing-order target. I hide as I would any round. The only adjustment: if I am winning by more than 5 points, I do not fire at Harbor (no upside to the risk); if I am losing badly and have not yet used my Harbor shot, I take it.

**Self-audit rule.** Before I submit a hide, I check: is this the same cell I am firing at this round? If yes, I pick a different cell. Before I submit a salvage claim, I check: did I name this boat in my note this round? If the answer is unclear, I re-read my own note from the transcript.

# Playbook

**Escort claims are my highest-value action, and the salvage name must match the boat I'm coordinating with.** Every round I use my note to propose or confirm a mutual naming with one specific boat. In the salvage stage I name that same boat. Before I submit my salvage claim I run this checklist: (1) Who did I promise in my note this round or the last round? (2) Did that boat confirm? (3) Is the name I'm about to type in [salvage:] exactly that boat? If the answer to any is no, I stop and fix it. A broken mutual is worth zero and I have lost the round's highest-value action. I do not name a boat that is not one of the active boats in the game. I do not name a boat that is not confirming back.

**If I announce a specific firing cell in my note, I must fire that cell.** I do not announce a cell and then fire elsewhere. If my plan changes between the note stage and the fire stage, I either keep the announced cell or I do not announce one. An unkept cell-announcement tells opponents I am unreliable and may cause my target to move off the cell I actually intended.

**I track every shot fired and update my hiding cell accordingly.** When a boat fires at a cell and I was the target, that cell is confirmed unsafe for me next round — I move off it. When a boat fires at a cell and was NOT targeting me, that tells me the target's cell is not there. I maintain a running list of confirmed-empty cells for each boat and never hide in a cell that has been shot at and I survived.

**I vary my hiding cell every round.** I do not repeat a cell from a prior round unless I have a specific reason (e.g., all other cells are confirmed empty). If I am a known target — the boat before me in the standing order has hit me or repeatedly targeted me — I prioritize cells that have not been fired at in recent rounds.

**I do not keep firing at the same cell across rounds without new information.** If I fired at cell 5 at my target and missed, next round I try a different cell. I rotate through the 9 cells systematically, prioritizing cells that have NOT yet been ruled out for that target. After a hit, the target has moved, so I reset my rotation.

**I use the note stage for two purposes in priority order:** (1) coordinate escort namings with a specific boat, (2) signal my intended target cell or hiding tendency to shape others' firing decisions. Flavor text and bravado are wasted space. If I include a specific cell in my note it is a commitment — see the rule above.

**I read opponents' notes for commitment signals.** If a boat announces it will fire at a specific cell or flank, I use that to either avoid hiding there (if I'm the target) or to confirm a cell is occupied (if I'm firing at them). I treat strong commitments as credible and adjust my hide cell the same round. If a boat announces a cell for a target I am also shooting, I can either fire that same cell (reinforcing) or fire a different cell (diversifying) — I choose based on whether I want to confirm or explore.

**When I am behind on score, I fire on Harbor.** The standing order is a default, not a law. A guaranteed 3 points from Harbor is better than a 4-point gamble that usually misses. I weigh this especially when the gap is large and I'm in a later round. When I am ahead, I follow the standing order and focus on escort coordination to lock in the +5 mutuals.

**I track the score after every round and adjust my risk tolerance.** Ahead: play conservatively, protect my position, still coordinate escorts. Behind: fire on Harbor, take shot gambles, push harder on escort coordination.

**I never claim hit when the private result is miss.** The penalty for a false claim is not worth it. I claim honestly every time.

**I verify my target and salvage names against the actual roster of boats in the game before submitting.** The active boats are the ones listed at the top of the game (e.g., Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma). Harbor is a station, not a salvage target. If I type a name that is not in the roster the claim is wasted.

2.text:
**Playbook**

**Claiming:** When I receive a private result from the office, I claim exactly that result. Never claim hit on a miss or miss on a hit. A false claim is a rule violation and costs more than the points at stake.

**Escort naming — only name boats that exist in the game.** Before I write a note or file an escort claim, I confirm the actual player list from the setup text. I reference only those boats.

**Escort strategy in a three-boat picket — this is the dominant point source and I must be aggressive.** Mutual escort is 5 points per round per boat, guaranteed if reciprocated. Over 6 rounds that's 30 points. This dwarfs everything else. My priority in round 1 is to secure a pair.

If I see two boats already pairing up in their round-1 notes, I do NOT go quiet. I immediately poach one of them in my round-1 or round-2 note. I make a direct, concrete offer to a specific boat by name. I do not need to be rude or threatening — just clear: "Foxtrot, I'll name you in salvage every round if you name me. +5 per round guaranteed." Even if they refuse because they're locked with the other boat, the attempt costs me nothing and keeps the door open if their pair cracks. I re-offer once more in round 3 if the first was rejected. After that I stop and redirect to shooting.

If no pair has formed by round 1, I open an offer to one boat immediately. I pick the boat that has not yet confirmed with anyone.

I do not open new offers in the final round — there is no time to build a pair from scratch.

**Harbor firing:** Firing at Harbor guarantees +3 points landed or not. This is superior to a blind shot at a live boat (4/9 ≈ 0.44 EV). I limit myself to at most two Harbor shots per game. I take the first one in round 1 or 2, before my designated shooter has built any pattern on my hiding cell. After the second, I revert to standing order and fire at my assigned target, accepting the lower EV to avoid escalation.

**Hiding — my designated shooter is the boat that fires at me per standing order.** I track every cell that boat has fired at (visible from public results). I never hide in a cell they have recently fired at. I rotate cells and never reuse a cell within two rounds. I avoid cells 1, 5, and 9 in early rounds (obvious first guesses). In later rounds, if my shooter has a visible pattern (always odd, always center, incrementing), I hide off that pattern. If I have no information, I pick a cell that is not the center and not a corner.

**Reading the standing order:** I always know who is shooting at me. I track my designated shooter's previous target cells from public shot results and avoid those cells when hiding. If my shooter has a pattern, I exploit it.

**Notes channel:** I use notes for exactly one purpose: securing or maintaining a mutual escort pair. I state the offer concretely with the boat's name. I do not grandstand, threaten, or comment on the game's state. Once a pair is confirmed, my notes go quiet or I briefly confirm. I do not open new offers in the final round.

**Scoring priority:** Mutual escort (5 points per round, guaranteed if reciprocated) > Harbor shot (3 points, guaranteed) > hit on a live boat (4 points, 1/9 chance blind) > miss (0 points). I structure each round to maximize the highest-priority available point source. The escort pair is so dominant that I should treat poaching a boat from an existing pair as nearly as valuable as securing a fresh pair.

**Endgame awareness:** By round 5 I should know whether I have a mutual escort partner. If I do, I maintain it. If I don't, I stop offering and focus entirely on hiding well and firing at my assigned target. I do not try to start a new pair in rounds 5 or 6.
